summary: Singleton toast queue: call Show("message") from anywhere and messages display one at a time.
overview: A short status message that appears, sits for a moment and goes away — "Saved", "Not enough gold", "Checkpoint reached". Call it from anywhere without holding a reference, and a burst of calls queues instead of stacking into unreadable overlapping text.
useCases: Confirming an action succeeded without interrupting the player with a dialog.
Surfacing a soft failure — a purchase you cannot afford, an inventory that is full.
Debug feedback during development, from systems that have no UI of their own.

params.why: The panel shown and hidden for each toast.
params.tuning: This component can sit on the panel itself — that is the normal setup and it is safe, because hiding is done with a CanvasGroup rather than by deactivating the object.

params.why: The TMP_Text the message is written into.
params.tuning: Left unwired, toasts still queue and time out correctly — you just never see the text. Nothing errors.

params.why: Seconds each toast stays up before the next one shows.
params.tuning: This is per message, so a queue of five at the default 2s takes 10 seconds to drain. Keep it short if bursts are likely.

usage.code:
ToastNotification.Instance.Show("Checkpoint reached");
ToastNotification.Instance.Show("Not enough gold");   // queues behind the first
usage.codeNote: No reference needed and no null check — Singleton<T>.Instance finds the one in the scene.

gotchas.title: Never hide the panel by deactivating its GameObject
gotchas.body: If this component sits on the panel it hides, deactivating that object breaks it twice over: Singleton<T>.Instance uses FindObjectOfType, which skips inactive objects, so Instance silently creates a SECOND empty ToastNotification with nothing wired and every Show() does nothing; and StartCoroutine cannot run on an inactive GameObject, so the queue never processes. It hides via a CanvasGroup for exactly this reason. This was a real bug, not a hypothetical.

gotchas.title: The queue is drained by a coroutine, so it needs Play mode
gotchas.body: Show() outside Play mode enqueues the message and nothing more — the coroutine that displays it never runs.

gotchas.title: Waiting is scaled time
gotchas.body: It waits with WaitForSeconds, so a toast shown while the game is paused with Time.timeScale = 0 stays up indefinitely. Pause menus that need toasts want an unscaled wait instead.
